scenes.visual: Title card 'Winning the First Hours' over a skin cut drawn as a simple box, a few GOLD dots inside. COLOUR MAP (both films): bacteria GOLD dots; removal dial and the letter k TEAL; barrier wall BROWN; macrophages and monocytes PURPLE; neutrophils BLUE; receptor sensor glow WHITE-YELLOW; complement C3b small GREEN tags; C3a and C5a ORANGE sparks; water flea drawn transparent GREY. Numbers appear only as on-screen text.

scenes.tts: A cut lets in one hundred bacteria, and each one doubles every twenty minutes. New antibodies take days, so what has to happen in the first few hours?
scenes.caption: A cut lets in 100 bacteria, and each one doubles every 20 minutes. New antibodies take days, so what has to happen in the first few hours?
scenes.visual: The wound box with 100 GOLD dots and a counter '100'. A clock face at top right reads 0:00. A calendar strip at the bottom is labelled 'new antibodies: days', far off to the right.
scenes.narration: A cut lets in 100 bacteria, and each one doubles every 20 minutes. New antibodies take days, so what has to happen in the first few hours?

scenes.tts: Start with no defense at all. Every twenty minutes, the count doubles. The clock runs for four hours, and the counter climbs past four hundred thousand.
scenes.caption: Start with no defense at all. Every 20 minutes, the count doubles. The clock runs for four hours, and the counter climbs past 400,000.
scenes.visual: GOLD dots split in pairs each tick; the box fills. Counter steps 100, 200, 400, 800 ... and lands on '409,600' as the clock reaches 4:00 ('12 doublings' on screen). Inset: a computed curve of count against time on a log axis, a straight rising GOLD line.
scenes.narration: Start with no defense at all. Every 20 minutes, the count doubles. The clock runs for four hours, and the counter climbs past 400,000.

scenes.tts: Now add a defense. In each doubling time, it removes a fraction of the bacteria. Call that fraction k. The survivors then double, just as before.
scenes.visual: Reset to 100. A TEAL dial labelled 'k = fraction removed per doubling time' appears beside the box. Each tick, a TEAL sweep removes some GOLD dots, then the survivors split in pairs.
scenes.narration: Now add a defense. In each doubling time, it removes a fraction of the bacteria. Call that fraction k. The survivors then double, just as before.

scenes.tts: So each doubling time multiplies the count by two times one minus k. That factor is the whole race. Above one, the count grows. Below one, it shrinks.
scenes.caption: So each doubling time multiplies the count by 2 × (1 − k). That factor is the whole race. Above 1, the count grows. Below 1, it shrinks.
scenes.visual: The factor '2 × (1 − k)' writes itself in TEAL and parks in the top-left corner for the rest of the film. A horizontal line at 'factor = 1' splits a panel into 'grows' above and 'shrinks' below.
scenes.narration: So each doubling time multiplies the count by 2 × (1 − k). That factor is the whole race. Above 1, the count grows. Below 1, it shrinks.

scenes.tts: Suppose the defenses remove three quarters of the bacteria every twenty minutes. Does the count rise or fall? Decide before the counter moves.
scenes.caption: Suppose the defenses remove three quarters (k = 0.75) of the bacteria every 20 minutes. Does the count rise or fall? Decide before the counter moves.
scenes.visual: Dial set to 'k = 0.75'. Counter frozen at 100 with a question card 'rise or fall?'.
scenes.narration: Suppose the defenses remove three quarters (k = 0.75) of the bacteria every 20 minutes. Does the count rise or fall? Decide before the counter moves.

scenes.visual: Predict pause. Question card holds; 5-second ring timer at bottom right.

scenes.tts: It falls. The factor is one half, so every twenty minutes the pile halves. After four hours, the expected count is far below one bacterium. The infection is very likely cleared.
scenes.caption: It falls. The factor is 1/2, so every 20 minutes the pile halves. After four hours, the expected count is far below one bacterium. The infection is very likely cleared.
scenes.visual: Corner factor fills in '2 × 0.25 = 0.5'. Counter steps down 100, 50, 25 ... to 'about 0.024 (expected count)'. Computed log-axis curve: a straight TEAL line falling, beside the GOLD no-defense line rising.
scenes.narration: It falls. The factor is 1/2, so every 20 minutes the pile halves. After four hours, the expected count is far below one bacterium. The infection is very likely cleared.

scenes.tts: Now slide the dial down. At exactly one half removed, the factor is one, and the counter freezes. So in this model, the rule is simple: remove more than half every doubling time.
scenes.caption: Now slide the dial down. At exactly half removed (k = 0.5), the factor is 1, and the counter freezes. So in this model, the rule is simple: remove more than half every doubling time.
scenes.visual: Dial slides from 0.75 to 0.5; the TEAL computed line pivots until flat at 100. Label 'k = 0.5: factor 1, holds'. Text 'win: k above 0.5' appears in TEAL.
scenes.narration: Now slide the dial down. At exactly half removed (k = 0.5), the factor is 1, and the counter freezes. So in this model, the rule is simple: remove more than half every doubling time.

scenes.tts: But when does the removal start? Keep the same strong defense, and make it wait one hour. The pile reaches eight hundred before it turns.
scenes.caption: But when does the removal start? Keep the same strong defense (k = 0.75), and make it wait one hour. The pile reaches 800 before it turns.
scenes.visual: Computed curve: GOLD rises for one hour to a peak labelled '800', then the TEAL defense switches on and the line falls. A bracket over the first hour reads 'delay 1 h'.
scenes.narration: But when does the removal start? Keep the same strong defense (k = 0.75), and make it wait one hour. The pile reaches 800 before it turns.

scenes.tts: Wait two hours, and it reaches six thousand four hundred. Each hour of waiting multiplies the pile eightfold. That is why the receptors must be ready before infection.
scenes.caption: Wait two hours, and it reaches 6,400. Each hour of waiting multiplies the pile eightfold. That is why the receptors must be ready before infection.
scenes.visual: A second computed curve with a 2-hour delay peaks at '6,400' above the first. Arrow between peaks '× 8 per hour of delay (3 doublings)'. Caption strip: 'illustrative model, not a measured wound'.
scenes.narration: Wait two hours, and it reaches 6,400. Each hour of waiting multiplies the pile eightfold. That is why the receptors must be ready before infection.

scenes.tts: In this model of a bacterial wound, the defenses we follow do three jobs. First, fewer get in. Skin and other barriers lower the starting number.
scenes.visual: A BROWN wall rises around the wound box; most GOLD dots bounce off, a few slip through a gap. Job card '1 fewer get in'. Small label: 'jobs this model follows; not a complete list'.
scenes.narration: In this model of a bacterial wound, the defenses we follow do three jobs. First, fewer get in. Skin and other barriers lower the starting number.

scenes.tts: Second, the clock starts early. A macrophage, a long-lived eating cell in the tissue, carries ready-made receptors. One, toll-like receptor four, senses a molecule from the outer membrane of many bacteria.
scenes.caption: Second, the clock starts early. A macrophage, a long-lived eating cell in the tissue, carries ready-made receptors. One, Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), senses a molecule from the outer membrane of many bacteria.
scenes.visual: A PURPLE macrophage sits in the box; a small block on its surface labelled 'TLR4' glows WHITE-YELLOW the instant a GOLD dot touches it (label 'lipopolysaccharide'). The clock face starts. Job card '2 the clock starts early'.
scenes.narration: Second, the clock starts early. A macrophage, a long-lived eating cell in the tissue, carries ready-made receptors. One, Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), senses a molecule from the outer membrane of many bacteria.

scenes.tts: Third, more are removed per doubling. Sensing sets off inflammation. A nearby vessel widens and leaks. Neutrophils pour out first, then monocytes, which become macrophages.
scenes.visual: A red vessel along the bottom of the box widens and gaps open; BLUE neutrophils squeeze out first and chase GOLD dots, then PURPLE monocytes follow and grow into macrophages. The TEAL dial ticks upward. Job card '3 more removed per doubling'.
scenes.narration: Third, more are removed per doubling. Sensing sets off inflammation. A nearby vessel widens and leaks. Neutrophils pour out first, then monocytes, which become macrophages.

scenes.tts: Inflammation runs in four steps: sense, vessels change, cells arrive, then clear and repair. As the eating cells gather, the fraction removed in each doubling time climbs.
scenes.visual: Four labelled blocks light in order: 'sense', 'vessels change', 'cells arrive', 'clear and repair'. Beside them the TEAL dial needle rises toward the 0.5 mark but stops short of it (schematic); small label 'whether it passes 0.5 depends on the infection'.
scenes.narration: Inflammation runs in four steps: sense, vessels change, cells arrive, then clear and repair. As the eating cells gather, the fraction removed in each doubling time climbs.

scenes.tts: Keep them out, see them at once, and remove more than half every doubling time. This is an illustrative model of one wound, not a measured infection.
scenes.visual: The three job cards line up beneath the wound box: BROWN wall, glowing TLR4 block, BLUE and PURPLE cells. Small text: 'illustrative model: one well-mixed wound, constant rates'.
scenes.narration: Keep them out, see them at once, and remove more than half every doubling time. This is an illustrative model of one wound, not a measured infection.

scenes.visual: End card with Hex, one line only: 'Remove more than half every doubling time, and start early.'
